subject.title: feat(feeds): search and follow signed publisher feeds

question: Should signed publisher discovery and durable publisher follows become an OpenClaw core workflow, or should this ClawHub-specific consumer be delivered as an owner plugin using a narrowly defined generic seam?
rationale: The answer fixes the public CLI, SQLite, upgrade, and long-term ownership contract; code review cannot safely choose it from implementation quality alone.

options.title: Route the consumer to an owner plugin
options.body: Keep any truly reusable signed-feed primitive generic in core, but move publisher CLI, protocol-specific transport, and follow state to a ClawHub-owned plugin or package.

options.title: Sponsor a generic core feed capability
options.body: Approve a scoped core design that names the plugin SDK seam, migration/upgrade contract, configuration ownership, and which provider-specific pieces remain outside core.

options.title: Pause pending protocol acceptance
options.body: Wait for the hosted-feed RFC and producer contract to settle before accepting persistent core state or a public CLI surface.

recommendation.title: Route the consumer to an owner plugin
recommendation.body: Keep any truly reusable signed-feed primitive generic in core, but move publisher CLI, protocol-specific transport, and follow state to a ClawHub-owned plugin or package.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed technical contact across the linked feed-stack commits; a repository owner still needs to make the final product decision.
